english.title: Proceeds of Crime - nominated officer consents to prohibited act
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being an officer nominated to receive disclosures under section 338 of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, knowing or suspecting that an act was prohibited, consented to the doing of that act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..), where none of the conditions in section 336(2), (3) or (4) was satisfied
english.legislation: Contrary to section 336 of theProceeds of Crime Act 2002.
english.pointstoprove:
being an officer nominated to receive disclosures
knowing/suspecting that an act was prohibited
consented to the doing of that act
which in the circumstances was prohibited
as not satisfying any of the conditions in section 336(2), (3) or (4)

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: MoPI group cannot be established from the offence code alone. Group 2 or 3 may apply depending on the nature of the related crimes. Manual MoPI review is required.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
